changes: Over $4bn ARR target moved from year-end to January, possibly end of February, after a Microsoft network change across 200 MW and supplier timing.
December quarter implied near $250mn of revenue, plus any residual mining (a quarter of $1bn ARR, no material new Horizon or Mackenzie capacity), against $392mn consensus dated 17 October.
FY27 capex plan cut: about $5bn spent plus about $15bn remaining, or near $20bn, against $25bn to $30bn in August.
New contracts at about $22mn per IT MW-year on five years and over $40mn on a short term; prepayments reach up to 90% of GPU capex.
Net debt rose from $216mn to $4.43bn in one quarter; parent-guaranteed GPU debt priced at 9.0% and 9.51%.

consensus_thesis: A former miner with owned power becoming a GPU cloud, with over $4bn of contracted ARR for 2026 capacity, where the market pays for the contracts but doubts the funding.
headline: The consensus view should shift from timing to funding: the $4bn ARR target slipped one to two months and December-quarter consensus needs to fall by about a third, but cutting FY27 capex by $5bn to $10bn and raising contract prices lowers the funding risk the stock had been pricing, while credit quality holds rather than improves as net debt jumps to $4.4bn.
kona: IREN's newest contracts show a tenant can fund up to 90% of GPU capex by prepayment, which sets the opening ask if Kona owns GPUs. Its 9.0% to 9.51% parent-guaranteed debt is the price of non-investment-grade GPU money, likely a floor for Kona. IREN's contract protects it from delay credits when Microsoft asks for a change, yet revenue still starts late; Kona should copy that clause and also seek payment for time lost to tenant changes. Staging capex with cheap land options is the behavior to copy.
monitor: Operating ARR and Horizon 2 to 4 acceptance dates by end January.
How the $6bn target funding closes, at what price, and ATM use with the stock near $21 (post-quarter sales averaged about $36).
Tenant, MW and term on 2027 contracts; operating margin as AI revenue ramps.

sections.body: Emphasized more: capital discipline (the CEO attributed the capex cut purely to financial markets), prepayment share, investment-grade share of backlog, data center assets as collateral ($6bn net, 20-year life). Emphasized less or dropped: the $25bn-$30bn FY27 capex headline; any dated target for ARR beyond the $4bn level (the CFO declined to give one). KPIs now matter more: remaining capex against sources, prepayment percentage, operating margin. Less: mining revenue ($28mn, ending by December). Risks up: delivery, refinancing load (current debt $950mn vs $169mn). Risks down: equity-at-any-price, since the capex plan flexed.

sections.body: Delay. Concern: the ARR ramp keeps moving. Response: tenant-requested and small. Evidence: 10-Q says Microsoft-requested changes extend delivery dates with no delay credits due; Horizon 3 GPUs on site, Horizon 4 still arriving. Funding. sections.title: Major risks

sections.body: What the next dollar costs: stated 9.0% and 9.51% on parent-guaranteed GPU debt (effective 10.7% and 10.4%), against stated 5.96% on non-recourse private-placement notes (effective 7.1%); converts effective 0.4% to 4.2%, with dilution. No market bond or CDS quote found. Maturities to June 2028: $723mn (rest of FY27), $1,059mn (FY28), against current debt of $950mn. GPU tranches amortize over 30 to 36 months, about the length of short contracts. Does the contract out-earn funding? At about $22mn per IT MW-year with 90% GPU prepayment, management cites 18-month GPU payback in a $20mn, 50% example; on those terms yes, but operating margin has yet to show it. Market cap near $8.9bn at $21.07 (24/7 Wall St., 6 Nov, 9:54 ET) on 424.4mn shares; remaining capex is 1.7x that.
sections.title: Capital and funding

sections.body: Signals: Operating ARR at 31 January; Remaining FY27 capex against closed funding; Share count against the ATM; Prepayment share on new contracts; AI cloud operating margin. Risks building: Current debt up more than fivefold to $950mn; $18.9bn of commitments, up from $13.8bn; 70% revenue with three customers. Confirmation: Horizon 2 to 4 accepted by February; data center financing closed without the parent; a named 2027 tenant. Tripwires: ARR past February; ATM use below $25 to fund capex; a new GPU debt coupon above 10%; any contract with prepayment under 50%.

rows: Credit. You have $5.8bn of cash, $2.3bn restricted, against $18.9bn of commitments. Which are cancellable, and what is the latest date you must close the $6bn before capex stops?
Tests P2. Not answered as framed.

Tests recourse. Sources named, price not.
Equity. You sold about $630mn of stock in October at about $36 by our math. Will you use the ATM near $21?
Dilution. Not asked as far as visible.
Equity. You estimate GPU useful lives and sign contracts for three to five years. What operating margin does Horizon 1 earn today?
Delivery. Microsoft's change extends dates without credits. How many more changes can it request and is any revenue date contractually fixed?
